problem: In the private load method `this.items` is assigned after `await` outside `runInAction`, while the next lines update `total` and `loading` inside one.
impact: MobX reports a strict-mode warning on every load, and observers render once with the new rows but the old total and a still-true loading flag before the second batch lands.

problem: The constructor creates a `reaction` on `page` and discards the returned disposer, so `dispose()` (which only drains `disposers`) never stops it.
impact: Every visit to the orders page leaves a live reaction that keeps the store and its up-to-2,000 loaded rows reachable after unmount, and repeated visits stack leaked stores.

problem: `loadOrders` sets `loading = true` but has no `finally`; the success path resets it and the catch path only sets `error`.
impact: When the request fails (timeout, 500) the table spinner never stops and covers the error, so support staff see an endless loading state until they reload the page.

problem: The truthy guard `status && ...` rejects `undefined`, so choosing the 'All statuses' option in the select never clears the status filter.
impact: After filtering by Paid the user cannot go back to all orders; the list stays on Paid and the select shows a cleared value that no longer matches the data.

problem: The private inter-store callback is declared as a decorated `@action.bound private` method; the project wants private methods as arrow fields and `@action.bound` only on public UI methods.
impact: Breaks the store convention and makes the class mix two binding styles, so readers cannot tell which private methods are actions.

problem: `onChangeQuery` is only called by the filter store through the constructor callback, never from JSX, yet it is public (no `private`).
impact: It widens the store's public API with an internal hook that components can call and that bypasses the filter store.

problem: The derived page total is a plain method that sums all items on each call instead of a `@computed` getter.
impact: OrdersSummary calls it in render, so with 2,000 rows the sum is recomputed on every selection change and re-render rather than cached.

problem: 'Select all on page' replaces the observable `selectedIds` array with a new one instead of using `.replace()` on the existing array.
impact: OrdersSummary subscribes with `observe(store.selectedIds)` once per store, so after Select all it listens to the discarded array and the 'Orders (N selected)' document title silently stops updating while the Selected statistic keeps changing.
